title: Probing and Manipulating Quantum Materials with Strong-field Terahertz and Mid-infrared Radiation
authors: S. J. Li, H. Y. Wu, S. J. Zhang, Y. T. Li
abstract: Emergent phenomena in quantum materials arise from interactions among different degrees of freedom. Identifying these interactions and establishing their roles in ordered states are central problems in condensed-matter physics and provide a basis for controlling material properties. Many relevant low-energy excitations and gaps lie in the terahertz (THz) and mid-infrared (MIR) range, where intense phase-stable fields can both interrogate nonlinear dynamics and drive selected degrees of freedom far from equilibrium. This review surveys recent progress in probing and manipulating quantum materials with strong-field THz and MIR radiation, with emphasis on nonlinear electronic dynamics, collective-mode coupling, symmetry-sensitive responses and field-induced changes in electronic structure and ordered states. Particular attention is given to developments enabled by the Synergetic Extreme Condition User Facility (SECUF).
summary: This review surveys how strong-field Terahertz and Mid-infrared radiation are used to probe and manipulate emergent phenomena in quantum materials. By employing nonlinear spectroscopy, researchers can access complex dynamics related to coupled electronic, lattice, and superconducting orders. The work highlights the potential of these techniques to control material properties by driving systems far from equilibrium.
main_problem: The central problem is identifying and controlling emergent phenomena in quantum materials by understanding the complex interactions among various degrees of freedom (charge, spin, orbital, lattice). This control is crucial for tailoring material properties.
main_result: Strong-field THz and MIR radiation can drive quantum materials far from equilibrium, allowing for the transient reshaping and manipulation of ordered electronic and lattice states.
method: The work reviews techniques using nonlinear THz/MIR spectroscopy, including 2D spectroscopy and time-resolved measurements, to probe these complex dynamics.
model_or_system: The study covers diverse quantum materials, including superconductors (cuprates, $	ext{MgB}_2$), topological insulators, ferroelectrics ($	ext{SrTiO}_3$), and semiconductors (GaAs). The physics involves coupled electronic, lattice, and superconducting order parameters.
key_observables: Nonlinear conductivity, order-parameter dynamics (e.g., Higgs mode), gap/spectral-weight transfer, and symmetry-sensitive responses.
important_parameters: Strong-field THz and Mid-infrared radiation intensity, frequency, and phase coherence.
main_assumptions: Linear spectroscopy is insufficient for disentangling complex interactions, and the analysis often relies on semiclassical or anharmonic potential expansions.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the frequency coverage of intense THz sources and detection methods. Figure 2 summarizes nonlinear THz spectroscopy paradigms, linking techniques (like THz-pump/THz-probe) to physical information (like gap dynamics).
paper_structure: The review surveys progress by first establishing the need to probe coupled degrees of freedom. It then details the experimental platforms (THz/MIR sources, detection) and progresses through specific physical phenomena, such as nonlinear electronic dynamics, collective mode coupling, and symmetry-sensitive responses.
why_interesting: The techniques described—using intense, tunable THz/MIR fields to drive systems nonlinearly—are highly relevant to open quantum systems and quantum optics, as they represent coherent, non-equilibrium driving protocols for many-body systems.
